verdicts.reason: A puts the 'Taste the Glow' CTA in the top-left corner, above the logo, product and headline, so the reading order is backwards. It also leaves the lower third as dead space with only a stray circle and microscopic legal text. B keeps a logical logo → product → headline → copy → CTA flow, but its left edges are ragged (logo, body and CTA start at different x positions), 'bottled.' runs nearly into the right edge, the CTA is small and the legal line is unreadably tiny.

A has the right order (logo, headline, copy, CTA, product), but the body copy sits over the decorative ochre circle, the left edges of the logo, text and CTA don't line up, there is a large empty gap between the CTA and the product, and the product crowds the small bottom circle. B is the same layout as pair 1 A: the CTA is pinned top-left ahead of everything else, which breaks the hierarchy, the bottom third is empty and the legal text is illegible.
